senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. מְטֵי)to reach; to find.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 1:1">B. Mets. I, 1</cite> <he>אניּ מְצָאתִיהָ</he> I found it.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 2a:6">Ib. 2ᵃ</cite> <he>הואי אמינא מאי מצאתיה ראיתיה וכ׳</he> I might have thought ‘I found it’ meant ‘I discovered it’, although he had not taken it up &c.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 2a:6">Ib.</cite>, a. e. <he>וּמְצָאתָהּ דאתאי לידיה וכ׳</he> ‘and which thou hast found’ (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:3">Deut. XXII, 3</cite>) means that it came into his possession.

Gitt. IX, 10 מ׳ בה דבר ערוה he discovered in her something disgraceful (infidelity); מ׳ אחרת וכ׳ he found another woman handsomer than she; a. fr.—מה מָצִינוּ ב־ … אף וכ׳ what do we find with regard to—? So also &c., i.e. as in the case of—, so &c. Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., ch. VIII, Par. 7 מה מצינו בהקטרה … אף מליקה וכ׳ as when burning (the sacrifice on the altar) the head is separated from the trunk, so when pinching the neck of the bird the head must be severed &c.; a. fr.—Part. pass. מָצוּי, f. מְצוּיָה; pl. מְצוּיִין; מְצוּיוֹת accessible, frequent; likely.

<cite ref="Arakhin 30b:75">Arakh. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>ומצא פרט למ׳</he> ‘and he find the means’ (<cite ref="Leviticus 25:26">Lev. XXV, 26</cite>), this excludes the case of the means being accessible, i.e. of one who had the means at the time being.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 27a:16">B. Mets. 27ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:3">Deut. XXII, 3</cite>, v. supra) <he>מי שאבודה הימנו ומ׳ אצל וכ׳</he> that which is lost to him but accessible to any body else; <he>אבודה הימנו ואינה מ׳ אצל וכ׳</he> lost to him and inaccessible to every one else (e. g. swept away by a flood).

<cite ref="Shabbat 151b:11">Sabb. 151ᵇ</cite> <he>עשה עד שאתה מוֹצֵא ומ׳ לך וכ׳</he> do good while thou findest (an opportunity), and it is possible to thee (thou hast the means), and thou art yet in thy own power (possessest thy faculties).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 86a:5">Snh. 86ᵃ</cite> <he>כי ימצא פרט למ׳</he> ‘if one be found stealing &c.’ (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 24:7">Deut. XXIV, 7</cite>), this excludes the case when the abducted and sold person was in his power (his own child &c.).
<cite ref="Deuteronomy 24:7">Ib.</cite> <he>כמצויין בידו דמי</he> the case is to be judged as if they (the children) had been in his possession.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 85:11">Gen. R. s. 85</cite> <he>השטר מ׳ להגבות</he> the note can be produced for collection, i.e. evidence can be found against us.
<cite ref="Gittin 2b">Gitt. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>אין עדים מ׳ לקיימו</he> no witnesses are to be had to identify it.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 18a:11">B. Mets. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>במקום שהשיירות מ׳</he> where caravans pass frequently.
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 1:1">Esth. R. to I, 1</cite>, v. <cite ref="D00493"><he>דִּידְכֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 1:1">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 21:9">Ps. XXI, 9</cite>) <he>תהא ידך מ׳ ליפרע מאויביך</he> thou shalt have the opportunity of punishing thy enemies.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 4a:7">B. Kam. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>הזיקה מ׳</he> the damage through it is frequent.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 60a">Ib. 60ᵃ</cite> <he>רוח מ׳</he> an ordinary wind, <he>רוח שאינה מ׳</he> an extraordinary wind; a. v. fr.
Gen. R. s. 85 שנִמְצְאוּ בגניבה who are caught at a theft; a. fr.—Esp. to turn out, to follow, to result.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 1:4">Ḥull. I, 4</cite> <he>נ׳ כשר וכ׳</he> the result is, what is legal in slaughtering is illegal in pinching.
<cite ref="Pesachim 25b">Pes. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>ונ׳ למד</he>, v. <cite ref="L00566"><he>לָמֵד</he> II</cite>.

Sifré Deut. 210 נִמְצִּינוּ למדים from which we can consequently derive.—Y. Pes. V, beg. 31ᶜ, a. fr. נִמְצֵאתָ אומר thou turnest out saying, i.e. the result is, consequently.—אם תִּימָּצֵי (תִּמָּצֵא) לומר (abbr. את״ל) if you will say.
<cite ref="Gittin 82b:11">Gitt. 82ᵇ</cite> <he>אם תמצא לומר איתא וכ׳</he> if you will adopt the opinion of &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 136a:10">Sabb. 136ᵃ</cite> <he>את״ל פליגי וכ׳</he> if you assume that they differ &c.; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Tosefta Ohalot 4:12">Tosef. Ohol. IV, 12</cite> <he>כשתמצא לומר וכ׳</he> if you assume &c.

senses.gloss: to furnish, provide with. Gen. R. l. c. נאבדו וה׳ הקב״ה וכ׳ they (the tokens) had been lost, and the Lord provided others instead.
units: <cite ref="Chagigah 5a:15">Ḥag. 5ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>תמצאן</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 31:21">Deut. XXXI, 21</cite>) <he>עבד שרבו מַמְצִיא וכ׳</he> what remedy is there for a slave for whom his master invents evils and troubles? <cite ref="Deuteronomy 31:21">Ib.</cite> <he>הממציא לו מעות לעני וכ׳</he> he who is ready to furnish the means (of his delivery) to the poor man in distress (by which the persecutor’s greed is increased); [Rashi: he who has money ready for the poor man in extreme distress, instead of helping him to a livelihood in due time].

<cite ref="Arakhin 30b:75">Arakh. 30ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 19:5">Deut. XIX, 5</cite>) <he>ומצא פרט לממציא את עצמו</he> ‘and it strikes’, this excludes the case of one who brings himself within the range of the missile (after it is started); <cite ref="Makkot 8a:13">Macc. 8ᵃ</cite>; a. e.
